title: Deep-sea fishing and Tal Farlow
summary: He fished off San Pedro to relax, and they talk of guitarist Tal Farlow, a fisherman and sign painter.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Did you ever used to go fishing, back
Did I go fishing?
Yeah.
Yes.
Because you were saying that -- the other day, like during the '50s and '60s out here you used to go off San Pedro, go out deep sea fishing.
Out here, yeah.
It's peaceful out on the ocean.

Oh, boy, it is. Very peaceful. That's why I used to go out there and just lay dead, you know? Although I wasn't dead, but I'd just lay there and had my hook, and someone would say, 'Hey, you got a bite. You got a bite.' I'd go over there and there'd be a fish on it.
It's a good way to relax.
Yeah. Took away a lot of thoughts, you know, staying out of devilment. And I got a lot of pleasure out of it because I like to fish, period. Every day I went out there I had a good time.
A lot of guitarists seem to like deep sea fishing.
Yeah.
Did you ever hear of Tal Farlow?
Oh, yes.
Yeah. He's a big fisherman. He goes
out a lot. He lives around Asbury Park.
He does?
Yeah.
I wondered what happened to him.
Well, you know, it got to be too much of a strain, apparently. You know, like he kind of backed away.
Oh, did he?
He has another job, you know, he paints signs.
Yeah.
On stores.
A sign painter.
A sign painter. So he had that to fall back on and I think he just got tired of the whole rat race, you know.
Yeah.
New York, and --
Well, you can't blame him. Sometimes, the way music was going, you know.
Yeah.
